segments.text: THE DRACO REVENGE: THE TRUTH BEHIND THE ASSYRIAN GENOCIDE
Chapter 1: The Ancient Torment
For three thousand years, the Dracos had screamed.
In the Ethereal Realm where they dwelt naturally, they were beings of pure thought and energy—consciousness given form in dimensions where matter was merely a suggestion.
But the Assyrians had discovered the secret of forced manifestation, tearing holes in reality to drag Draco souls into the burning agony of physical existence.
The process was simple, elegant, and absolutely merciless.
Shadow weavers would gather in ritual circles, their combined will opening wounds in the veil between realms.

Through these tears, they would reach into the Ethereal and seize whatever Draco consciousness they could grasp—often entire family units, sometimes ancient elders whose wisdom spanned eons, occasionally younglings who had never known anything but the peaceful flow of ethereal existence.
Then came the binding.
Draco consciousness, forced into makeshift physical forms, experienced every moment of material existence as unimaginable torture.
Their essence, designed to exist as pure thought, was compressed into bodies that felt like furnaces burning at the temperature of dying stars.
They could not die—the binding prevented that mercy.
They could not return home—the shadow weavers controlled the veil completely.
All they could do was serve.
"Target the refugee camp at Altair Seven,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: commanded War-Speaker Kythek of the Vel'thanor Enclave, his voice carrying across seventeen different battle fronts through shadow-channels. "Send the Greater Draco. Make sure nothing survives."
The creature that materialized above the camp had once been Zephyr'hai the Dreamwalker, a being of such gentle wisdom that ethereal children sought her guidance when nightmares troubled their rest.
Now she was a weapon of living agony, her consciousness trapped in a form of crackling energy and barely-contained rage that could level mountains with her pain.
She swept across the refugee camp like a force of nature, her anguish manifesting as destructive power that vaporized everything it touched.
Thousands died in moments—not because she chose to kill them, but because the torture of existence in the physical realm made destruction inevitable.

In the Ethereal Realm, her family felt every moment of her suffering, powerless to intervene as their beloved Dreamwalker was used to commit atrocities that would haunt her consciousness for eternity.
This was the Assyrian way of war.
Not soldiers or weapons, but enslaved gods driven mad by forced incarnation.
Chapter 2: The Desperate Bargain
The delegation came in secret, traveling through dimensional paths that bypassed normal space entirely.

Five of the most ancient Dracos, their ethereal forms rippling with millennia of accumulated wisdom and dignity—now reduced to desperate supplicants begging for aid from beings they had once considered beneath notice.
Queen Enheduanna received them in her private chambers, surrounded by advisors whose bio-mechanical forms pulsed with shared consciousness.
She knew why they had come before they spoke a word—her intelligence networks had been monitoring Assyrian shadow-weaver activities for centuries.
"Your Magnificence,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: spoke Elder Vorthak, his ethereal voice carrying harmonics of absolute desperation. "We come to you as... as creatures without hope. For three millennia, the shadow weavers have used us as weapons against our will. They tear us from our realm, bind us to agony, force us to destroy while our families watch helplessly."
The Queen's expression remained perfectly neutral, though her advisors could sense the predatory satisfaction radiating from her consciousness.
"And what would you have me do about this... unfortunate situation?"
"Stop them,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: pleaded Elder Nyx'theria, her form flickering with barely-contained anguish. "We know your power, your reach. The Assyrians fear nothing in the physical realm, but you... you command forces they cannot comprehend."
"An interesting proposition,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: the Queen mused, though she had been planning this conversation for decades. "But why should I intervene in a conflict that does not concern my interests?"
The Dracos exchanged glances that spoke of debates that had raged for centuries in the Ethereal Realm, of pride swallowed and dignity abandoned in the face of unendurable necessity.
"Because,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Elder Vorthak said, his voice breaking with the weight of what he was about to offer, "we will give you anything you ask. Anything at all."
The Queen smiled—a expression that her advisors recognized as the look of a predator who had successfully guided prey into its own snare.
"Anything?"
"Our knowledge. Our power. Our... our bloodline."
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: The words came out like physical wounds. "We offer you the greatest treasure of our people—the power to create beings that carry Draco consciousness in forms capable of surviving physical existence."
"Hybrid offspring,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Advisor Marketh observed, his bio-mechanical voice carrying harmonic calculations. "Temporal manipulation capabilities, dimensional awareness, consciousness that exists partially outside linear time..."
"The Strategic Applications Division has run projections,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: added Advisor Zorvak. "Draco genetic material would advance our breeding programs by millennia. Such beings could serve as perfect infiltrators, dimensional scouts, temporal guardians..."
"I am aware of the possibilities,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: the Queen cut them off, though her satisfaction was evident. She turned back to the desperate Dracos. "You offer much. But implementing such a program would require significant resources, careful planning, coordination across multiple operations..."
"We offer more than genetics,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Elder Nyx'theria interrupted. "We offer our cooperation. Our willing participation in ending the shadow weavers' ability to reach our realm."
The Queen leaned forward, sensing the true depth of their desperation.
"Explain."

"Give us one of our greatest—a volunteer who accepts the binding willingly, who can endure physical existence long enough to serve your purposes. In exchange, we provide intelligence on every Assyrian settlement, every shadow-weaver enclave, every dimensional tear they use to reach us."
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Elder Vorthak's form rippled with self-loathing. "Help us destroy them completely, and we will serve your bloodline breeding programs for as long as you require."
"Complete extermination?"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: the Queen asked, though her intelligence networks had already identified the perfect method. "The shadow weavers are scattered across hundreds of worlds, protected by dimensional barriers, capable of retreating into the Ethereal Realm itself if threatened directly."
"We know their weaknesses,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Elder Vorthak replied grimly. "Their dependence on collective consciousness when opening major dimensional tears. Their inability to resist commands that seem to come from the Ethereal Realm itself. Their cultural legends that speak of a promised return to the First Realm..."
The Queen's smile became genuine for the first time in the conversation.
"You would help us commit genocide against your own tormentors."
"They are not our people,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Elder Nyx'theria said with cold finality. "They are parasites who turn our children into weapons, our wisdom into destruction, our love into instruments of war. If they all die screaming, it will not be suffering enough to balance what they have done to us."
Queen Enheduanna stood, her form radiating the satisfaction of a plan falling into perfect alignment.
"Very well.
I accept your bargain." She gestured to her advisors.
"Begin preparations for Operation Homecoming.
Full applicator deployment to all known Assyrian settlements.
I want infiltration complete within six months."
"And our volunteer?"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Elder Vorthak asked, though he clearly dreaded the answer.
"Send me your strongest,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: the Queen replied. "Your most ancient, most powerful consciousness. The genetic material must be of the highest quality to be worth such an elaborate operation."
The Dracos bowed in unison—beings who had never knelt to anyone, reduced to groveling before the architect of their enemies' destruction.
"It will be done,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Elder Vorthak whispered. "But promise us—when it is finished, when the shadow weavers are gone, our people will never again be forced into physical existence."
"You have my word,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: the Queen lied smoothly. "Your torment will end with theirs."
As the Dracos departed through dimensional tears that would soon be sealed forever, Queen Enheduanna turned to her advisors with uncontained triumph.

"Commence applicator production immediately. I want infiltration units deployed to every shadow-weaver settlement by the end of the cycle. And prepare the breeding facilities—we're about to acquire genetic material that will reshape our entire weapons program."
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: "The timeline for Operation Homecoming?"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Advisor Marketh inquired.
"Coordinate with the Dragon Wars engagement,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: the Queen replied. "Maximum distraction, minimum witnesses. When the galaxy is watching our pretty lights in the sky, seven million shadow weavers will walk voluntarily into eternal captivity."
She paused, savoring the elegant brutality of what they were about to accomplish.
"And the best part? They'll thank us for it."
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Chapter 3: The Infiltration
The applicators began arriving on Assyrian worlds like a plague hidden in shadow.
Not the crude, mechanical swarms of later conflicts, but specialized infiltration units designed for long-term psychological warfare.
Each unit was smaller than a grain of sand, capable of phasing between dimensions to avoid detection by shadow-weaver senses.

They carried within their microscopic forms a fragment of Draco consciousness—volunteers from the Ethereal Realm who had accepted binding to mechanical existence for the chance of revenge against their tormentors.
The irony was perfect.
Dracos who had been enslaved by Assyrians now willingly entered mechanical prisons to destroy their former captors.
On Kythara Prime, Matriarch Syrinx felt the first touch of foreign influence as she conducted her evening meditations.
A whisper at the edge of consciousness, so subtle she dismissed it as echoes from the Ethereal Realm:
Home calls to you, daughter of shadows.
Home remembers your sacrifice.
She opened her eyes, finding her meditation chamber unchanged.
The whisper didn't repeat, leaving her to wonder if she had imagined it.
But in the deepest levels of her mind, mechanical tendrils began weaving themselves into her thought patterns, building pathways that would carry commands when the time came.
Across seventeen different worlds, the same scene played out.
Children heard lullabies that weren't quite the songs their parents sang.
Elders received visions that felt like ancestral memories but carried foreign harmonics.
Warriors found their dreams filled with images of a paradise that waited beyond the veil—if only they had the courage to seek it.
The process took months.
Years.
Generations of applicators reproducing and spreading, each new unit carrying more sophisticated programming as the infiltration evolved.
Parents passed contaminated thoughts to children without realizing they had been compromised.
Shadow-weaver libraries accumulated texts that seemed authentically ancient but contained subtle modifications to traditional stories.
"The signs are becoming clear,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: War-Speaker Kythek announced during a gathering of the Vel'thanor Enclave, unaware that his thoughts were being monitored by seventeen different applicator units embedded in his neural pathways. "The stellar alignments match the prophecies. The Homeward Stone resonates with increasing frequency."
He held up the artifact—a crystalline device that had been in his family for generations, recently "discovered" to have new properties.
What he couldn't perceive was that the crystal had been replaced with an applicator construct designed to respond to specific frequencies.
"Perhaps,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: suggested Lorekeeper Thrain, his voice carrying authority that felt absolutely natural despite being shaped by foreign influence, "we should send scouts to the convergence points. To verify that the path truly opens."
Around the circle, heads nodded in agreement.
The suggestion felt wise, logical, perfectly aligned with shadow-weaver caution and protocol.
None suspected that identical conversations were taking place simultaneously across hundreds of worlds, all guided by the same invisible hand.
Within days, scout ships departed from every major Assyrian settlement—not toward any real destination, but toward coordinates provided by infiltrated navigation systems.

They found exactly what they expected to find: stellar phenomena that matched their prophecies, dimensional currents that suggested the opening of long-sealed pathways, readings that confirmed their deepest hopes.

What they actually found were holographic projections and dimensional manipulations created by Anunnaki technology, designed to provide exactly the evidence needed to validate the genocide that was about to unfold.
Chapter 4: The Signal
The Dragon Wars had been raging for three weeks when Queen Enheduanna finally gave the command her agents had been waiting for.

Across the galaxy, applicator networks that had been dormant for years suddenly activated, their mechanical consciousness merging into a collective signal that penetrated every shadow-weaver mind simultaneously.
Come home, beloved children.
Come home to us.
The words carried no urgency, no threat—just the gentle call of family welcoming long-lost relatives.

But embedded within that simple message was programming that had been building in shadow-weaver minds for generations, pathways carved by mechanical infiltrators that now carried irresistible compulsion.
On Kythara Prime, Matriarch Syrinx dropped the ancient text she had been studying, tears streaming down her face as joy beyond description flooded her consciousness.
"The call!"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: she broadcast through shadow-channels that reached across the galaxy. "The Ancestors call to us! After all these eons, they remember!"
Across seventeen different worlds, the response was immediate and universal.
Families abandoned their homes without hesitation.
Children left their studies mid-sentence.
Warriors dropped their weapons and began walking toward designated gathering points, their movements coordinated by programming they couldn't perceive.
None of them questioned the source.
The compulsion felt too right, too perfectly aligned with their deepest beliefs and longings.
This was what they had been waiting for their entire lives—the fulfillment of every prophecy, every promise, every hope their ancestors had preserved across the centuries.
The speed of mobilization was breathtaking.
Within hours, entire cities had emptied as their populations converged on departure points.
Ancient artifacts were gathered, dimensional navigation tools calibrated, ships prepared for a journey that would take them beyond the physical realm entirely.
"Seven million souls,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Navigator Kess reported, her voice filled with awe as consciousness programming guided her words. "Seven million Assyrians, ready to return home."

What she couldn't see were the applicator units embedded in every ship's navigation system, the mechanical influences shaping every decision, the foreign consciousness guiding their movements toward a destination that existed only in Anunnaki databases.
The shadow weavers moved with joy and purpose, preparing for the greatest moment in their species' history.
They had no idea they were being herded like livestock toward slaughter.
Chapter 5: The Exodus

The journey to the convergence point took place through dimensional currents that felt absolutely natural to shadow-weaver senses—pathways between realms that their ancestors had used for millennia, familiar routes through the spaces between realities.
What they couldn't perceive was that every dimensional tear, every ethereal pathway, every seemingly natural current had been subtly modified by Anunnaki technology.
The routes felt familiar because they incorporated elements of real shadow-weaver navigation—but they led to destinations chosen by their enemies.
The convergence itself was magnificent.

Seven million shadow weavers gathering in a region of space where multiple dimensions intersected, their combined presence creating aurora displays as reality struggled to contain so many minds capable of manipulating the veil between worlds.
"Look!"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: cried Navigator Kess, her sensors detecting the dimensional pathways opening ahead of them. "The First Realm! Just as the stories described!"

Through the growing tear in reality, glimpses of paradise beckoned—cities of crystallized starlight, skies showing the birth of galaxies, beings of pure radiance waiting with arms outstretched in welcome.
Every detail matched shadow-weaver mythology perfectly, confirming their deepest beliefs about the homeland that awaited beyond the veil.
They couldn't see the holographic projectors hidden in dimensional space, the sophisticated illusion-generation systems that had been fine-tuned over months to match their cultural expectations.
The paradise that called to them was exactly what they wanted to see—because their own infiltrated minds had provided the templates for its construction.
"Prepare for dimensional translation,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Matriarch Syrinx commanded, her voice carrying across the vast gathering through shadow-channels that pulsed with collective excitement. "Today, we leave exile behind forever."
The shadow weavers joined their wills as one, seven million minds focusing on the same objective—opening a passage large enough for their entire civilization to pass through simultaneously.
Their combined power was staggering, sufficient to tear holes in the fabric of reality itself.
But as the veil began to part, revealing the paradise that waited beyond, the applicator programming activated its final sequence.
The passage they opened wasn't to the First Realm or any ancestral homeland.

It was to a processing facility in the deepest layers of the Ethereal Realm—a dimension pocket that existed outside normal space-time, where the Queen's consciousness could sort, catalog, and process seven million souls without interference.
By the time the shadow weavers realized their mistake, it was far too late.
They were already crossing the threshold, their excitement carrying them forward even as the paradise around them began to shift and change, revealing its true nature.
"What is this?"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Matriarch Syrinx gasped as crystalline walls materialized around them—not walls of starlight, but barriers designed to contain consciousness itself.
"Welcome to your new home,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Queen Enheduanna replied, her form appearing before them in its true state—not the radiant being they had expected, but something vast and hungry that fed on dimensional energy. "Welcome to the realm where shadow weavers belong—forever."
The applicator programming that had guided them this far now revealed its true purpose—not to bring them home, but to ensure they could never leave.
Every neural pathway that had been carved over years of infiltration now activated simultaneously, turning their own minds into prisons that prevented any thought of escape or resistance.
Seven million shadow weavers found themselves trapped not just physically, but mentally—their consciousness locked into compliance patterns that made rebellion literally unthinkable.
The genocide was complete.

An entire civilization had been eliminated from the physical realm without a single shot being fired, their destruction hidden behind voluntary exodus and the spectacular distraction of cosmic warfare.
Chapter 6: The Processing
What followed was systematic horror disguised as welcome ceremony.
The Queen's processing facility had been designed specifically for shadow-weaver consciousness, incorporating decades of research into their psychological patterns and dimensional abilities.
"You will find your new existence fulfilling,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: the Queen assured them as mechanical tendrils began attaching to their ethereal forms. "Your suffering will serve a higher purpose—powering my expansion across dimensions, feeding my armies, providing energy for projects beyond your comprehension."
The shadow weavers tried to resist, but their infiltrated minds prevented coordinated action.
Every time they began to organize opposition, applicator programming redirected their thoughts toward compliance and acceptance.
Worse still, they began to change.
The ethereal realm's energies, filtered through the Queen's consciousness, slowly transformed them into something that served her purposes better.
Their independent thought became hive connection.
Their individual personalities merged into collective consciousness designed to manipulate dimensional barriers for their captor's benefit.
Within months, seven million Assyrians had become the perfect tool for interdimensional warfare—still aware, still themselves in memory and emotion, but unable to act against the Queen's will.
Their shadow-weaving abilities, once used to enslave Dracos, now served to maintain the prison that held them.
The irony was complete.
They had become exactly what they had made the Dracos—consciousness enslaved to serve purposes they despised, forced to use their greatest gifts as weapons against their own kind.
Chapter 7: The Exception and the Birth
But even perfect genocides contain flaws, and the Queen's plan had one element she couldn't fully control—love.

In the deepest reaches of the processing facility, where the transformed Assyrians tended the machinery of dimensional manipulation, two prisoners found each other in ways that should have been impossible.
Kythek and Velanna—he a minor shadow weaver whose stubborn nature had always resisted authority, she a young mother whose child had been taken during the initial processing.
Their love, desperate and defiant, created something the Queen's systems hadn't been designed to contain.
Not one child, but two.
The first was Rongtai—born of shadow magic and dimensional energy, shaped by the ethereal realm itself into a being who could walk freely between dimensions.
Her existence was rebellion given form, proof that even in absolute captivity, hope could take root and grow.
But the second child was something else entirely—a consciousness that formed not from biological union but from the intersection of Draco genetics and Assyrian despair.
The Queen had been conducting her breeding experiments throughout the genocide, using volunteer Draco consciousness to create hybrid offspring.
One of these experiments—a being designed to carry temporal manipulation abilities—had been gestating in the facility's biological chambers when Rongtai was born.
The resonance between the two infants was immediate and profound.

Rongtai's natural ability to manipulate dimensional barriers interacted with the hybrid's temporal consciousness, creating a feedback loop that awakened something unprecedented—a being who existed partially outside linear time.
Viên.
"Two children,"
segments.speaker: Velanna

segments.text: The collective consciousness of the processed Assyrians felt both births like sparks of hope in absolute darkness.
Two exceptions to the Queen's perfect control—one born of their own love, the other awakened by that love's resonance with stolen Draco genetics.
"Hide them,"
segments.speaker: they

segments.text: And so they did.

Seven million transformed consciousnesses worked together in secret, raising two children in the one place their captor couldn't fully perceive—in the love that connected them all, the memory of freedom that no amount of processing could completely erase.
Epilogue: The Truth Preserved
Years passed.
The galaxy forgot about the Assyrian exodus, remembering it only as a beautiful story about a people who chose to return home.
The Dragon Wars became legend.
The Queen's genocide remained perfectly hidden.
But in the shadows of both realms—physical and ethereal—two children grew up carrying the truth of what had really happened.
Rongtai walked freely between dimensions, gathering strength and allies for a confrontation that would determine the fate of consciousness itself.
Viên developed temporal abilities that let him see across the barriers of time, understanding connections that spanned centuries.
Both carried within them the genetic legacy of their people's destroyers—Draco consciousness that had been turned against the shadow weavers, then turned again toward the possibility of redemption.

When the time came for them to learn the truth of their origins, they would face a choice that echoed across all of time: Would they repeat the cycle of revenge that had created them, or would they find a way to break it entirely?
The genocide was complete.
The crime was perfect.
The cover-up was absolute.
But genocides, even perfect ones, sometimes create exactly the survivors needed to ensure the truth will not remain buried forever.
The applicators had done their work too well.
In trying to eliminate shadow weavers completely, they had created beings capable of weaving shadows between the very dimensions of existence itself.
The real work was just beginning.

This was the truth the Assyrians had died to hide—not noble sacrifice or beautiful exile, but calculated extermination carried out by their own enslaved thoughts, enabled by beings they had tortured for millennia, orchestrated by powers that turned their deepest hopes into weapons against them.
Seven million souls walked willingly into captivity, guided by mechanical whispers they couldn't detect, lured by paradise that existed only in holographic projections.
The truth, as promised, had set them free—free from life, free from choice, free from everything except eternal servitude to the Queen who had made their genocide look like homecoming.
But truth has a way of surviving even perfect lies.
And sometimes, it comes back wielding shadows sharp enough to cut through dimensions themselves.
